ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's domestic UAF/RP sanctions and caution lists. Enhanced due diligence required for all domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Continuous risk-based transaction monitoring under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Rule 004-2017. Negative news and adverse media screening is mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Portal de Servicios Electrónicos (Electronic Registry Portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation corporate name must be in Spanish or, if in a foreign language, must be easily romanized/transliterated into the Latin alphabet. Chinese characters or non-Latin scripts may appear only as a secondary commercial alias, not as the statutory registered name. The name must be distinguishable from any existing registered entity and must include the denomination 'Fundación' (Foundation), subject to permitted abbreviations and stylistic formats.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registrant or registered agent must file a written appeal (Recurso de Reconsideración) with the Registro Público de Panamá, within 5 business days, citing the rejection reference, revised name, and legal argument on distinctiveness. If reconsideration is denied, the Registro must issue a formal denial resolution, after which the appellant may file an appeal to the Superior Court (Tribunal Superior) as an administrative contentious proceeding. During appeal, an alternative name may be simultaneously reserved while preserving the original priority date only if the original name is under judicial contest.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is generally permissible for Private Interest Foundations as the registered agent's office may serve as the registered office. However, for the underlying physical grocery retail business to be carried out in Panama, a physical commercial premise is mandatory. Virtual office may not be used for the substantial retail operations where MINSA and municipal inspections apply. The foundation itself may be substance-light if adequately documented.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the foundation itself; Moderate-High (approximately 55-65%) for the physical grocery retail premises due to MINSA health inspections, municipal tax verification, and labor inspections by MITRADEL. Random commercial registration compliance visits by Registro Público are possible but less frequent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended, and its implementing Executive Decree No. 63 of 20 June 1996; statutory references: Articles 1-45 (constitution, council, protector, beneficiaries, and registration duties).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) - Foundations Section (Sección de Fundaciones)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation of a Private Interest Foundation (Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital; customary declared initial endowment of USD 10,000.00. Law No. 25 of 1995 imposes no escrow account requirement; the endowment is recorded as a written declaration in the Foundation Charter and must be available for the stated non-profit or reserved purposes of the grocery retail activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the duly convened first meeting of the Foundation Council of the Foundation, as follows: FIRST, the initial endowment of Ten Thousand United States Dollars (USD 10,000.00) subscribed by the Founder is hereby irrevocably accepted and recorded as the Foundation's patrimony. SECOND, the registered address is fixed at the Resident Agent's office in Panama. THIRD, three Councillors are appointed, with a designated President and Secretary. FOURTH, the Foundation Regulations (Reglamento) are adopted. FIFTH, the President and Secretary are jointly authorized to execute banking, contractual, and licensing documents, including the municipal Aviso de Operación, sanitary permit, and the tax registration forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría del Circuito) in joint coordination with the appointed Resident Agent law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian licensed attorney to draft the Public Deed of Incorporation identifying the Founder, the initial endowment, the business purposes (retail of imported Asian condiments and vegetables, ISIC 4721), the Foundation Council (minimum three members), the beneficiaries, and the Resident Agent. Execute the Deed before a Notary Public and obtain the First Testimony (Primer Testimonio) with notarial certification.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of the Founder and all Councillors
Signed acceptance letter of the Resident Agent
Original draft Charter with annexed Foundation Regulations
Proof of payment of notarial fees and fiscal stamps
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary Public objects to any clause (e.g., unlawful purpose or defective council composition), counsel revises and re-executes the Deed; if fiscal stamp deficiency is detected, pay the outstanding stamp tax and re-present for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones (Public Registry of Panama, Foundations Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the First Testimony and one certified copy with the Registry. The Registry assigns a foundation folio number, verifies the legal capacity and council composition, and issues the Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Inscripción). Pay the registration fee at the designated cashier window or through the STAAPS online payment portal and secure the stamped receipt.
required_dossiers: First Testimony of the Public Deed of Incorporation
Registry fee payment receipt
Beneficial ownership due-diligence form (Formulario de Titularidad / Ley 23 of 2015 filing)
Letter of instruction from the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'Vista Fiscal' or a defect notice (nota de defecto), the Resident Agent corrects the instrument or submits supplementary explanations within five business days; an appeal may be lodged with the Director of the Registry if the defect is deemed unfounded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Municipal Notice of Operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipalidad de Panamá (Alcaldía de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Registry-issued Foundation Certificate to the DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). Thereafter, file the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) with the Panama Municipality, declaring the commercial activity as specialized grocery retail (ISIC 4721) and paying the municipal fixed fee based on declared patrimony. Display the municipal operating badge at the physical premises.
required_dossiers: Foundation Registration Certificate issued by the Public Registry
RUC certificate obtained from DGI
Lease contract or title of the commercial premises
Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality assigns an incorrect activity code, submit the ISIC 4721 reference and the lease contract for reclassification; if the Aviso is placed in observation, amend the declared gross receipts projection within ten business days and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sanitary Operating Permit from the Ministry of Health
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Regional Health Directorate of the district where the supermarket premises are located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento (Sanitary Operating Permit) application for a food retail establishment, detailing storage areas for imported Asian condiments, chilled vegetables, and dry goods. A MINSA health inspector verifies refrigeration temperature logs, pest-control contracts, employee food-handling credentials, and waste separation practices. Pay the annual sanitation fee upon approval.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Aviso de Operación approved by the Municipality
Food handler certificates (carné de manipulador de alimentos) for all staff
Detailed floor plan and storage layout
Potable water quality analysis report or municipal supply bill
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection reveals deficiencies, the establishment is granted a corrective term of five to fifteen days; after remediation, request a re-inspection. If the permit is denied or suspended without cause, an appeal may be filed with the MINSA Regional Legal Department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (National Fire Department) and Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange a fire safety inspection of the retail premises confirming the presence of serviceable extinguishers, emergency exits, illuminated signage, and compliant electrical installations; obtain the Fire Department Inspection Certificate (Certificado de Inspección). Register the establishment with MITRADEL as an employer under Law No. 55 of 2003 and obtain the occupational health and safety clearance for the workplace.
required_dossiers: Lease contract of the commercial premises
Approved Aviso de Operación
Fire extinguisher maintenance and service contracts
Employee payroll and headcount list
Civil liability and property insurance policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Fire Department issues observations, correct the flagged conditions and pay the re-inspection fee. MITRADEL queries are cured by submitting the missing payroll, the workplace risk assessment, or the adopted internal safety regulation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Categorization and Waste Management Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Seguridad Ambiental
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Environmental Categorization Application through the SINIA system for retail food sales at a fixed physical premises. The establishment will be classified as Categoría I (minor impact) given the limited footprint, absence of significant industrial discharge, and use of municipal water and sewerage; obtain the Certificado de Categorización Ambiental. Execute a solid-waste collection service contract with an authorized municipal or private hauler.
required_dossiers: Environmental categorization application form (SINIA/DGSA)
Location plan and neighborhood context map
Description of refrigeration equipment and refrigerants
Solid-waste hauling service contract (if applicable)
Approved Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MiAMBIENTE elevates the classification to Categoría II, the Foundation must prepare a simplified Environmental Impact Assessment (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Categoría II) through a licensed consultant within sixty days; if the categorization is challenged erroneously, submit documentary evidence of domestic-equivalent wastewater and retail-only operations to the Dirección de Seguridad Ambiental.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) in coordination with the Municipalidad de Panamá (Alcaldía de Panamá)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Notice of Operation) for Retail Grocery - ISIC 4721, combined with the Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento (MINSA Sanitary Operating Permit)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Seguridad Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I - Environmental Categorization Certificate (full EIA not required) for a retail grocery premises operating on municipal water and sewer; Categoría II would apply only if the premises adds commercial cold-storage processing, substantial refrigeration compressors above threshold, or food-manufacturing lines.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the Reglamento de Descargas de Aguas Residuales (ANAM/MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0357-2019): pH between 6.5 and 8.5, BOD5 not exceeding 350 mg/L, COD not exceeding 700 mg/L, and total suspended solids not exceeding 300 mg/L. Solid waste must be segregated and disposed in accordance with Ley No. 38 of 2005, while commercial refrigeration equipment must phase out HCFC (R-22) refrigerants in line with Panama's national ozone-depleting substances schedule.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá verifying fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and electrical compliance; municipal structural load inspection of the premises; and MITRADEL occupational clearance under Law No. 55 of 2003, including workplace risk assessment, employee hygiene training, and compliance with MINSA public-health protocols for grocery retail operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; official taxpayer portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (e-Tax 2.0 for filings and SIFE electronic invoicing web services).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) operating a retail grocery business: (1) Execute the PIF charter before a Panamanian notary, declaring an initial endowment (customarily at least B/. 10,000) and appointing the statutorily required resident agent (abogado idóneo); (2) inscribe the foundation in the Registro Público and obtain the certificate of legal existence; (3) before commencing retail activity, obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación; (4) apply to DGI for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) in the legal-entity registration module of e-Tax 2.0, attaching the foundation certificate, charter, resident-agent affidavit, and the Aviso de Operación; (5) upon approval, receive the permanent RUC, which simultaneously registers the foundation for the ITBMS (VAT) and obliges enrollment in SIFE for real-time electronic invoicing. The RUC/TIN is mandatory for supplier contracting, customs import clearance, bank account opening, and all ISR/ITBMS declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Panama; the PIF is an opaque taxable person under domestic law. Statutory elections relevant to this retail operation include: (i) the small-taxpayer fixed-quota regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente), available where annual gross income does not exceed B/. 300,000; (ii) the foundation charter election between passive asset administration and active commercial activity, which becomes mandatory ISR/ITBMS compliance once retail trade is conducted; (iii) consolidated ISR filing for qualifying Panamanian corporate groups with prior MEF authorization under the Código Fiscal; and (iv) documentary exclusion of foreign-source receipts from the territorial IR-1 return without any formal transparency election.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No independent Panamanian central bank is constituted. Monetary policy is delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve under de jure dollarization. The banking and foreign-exchange supervisory function is performed by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); the Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent, clearing house and banker to the Government, issuing the fractional Balboa coins only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama grants unrestricted legal tender to the U.S. dollar; the Panamanian balboa (PAB) is purely a fractional unit pegged 1:1 to USD. Both current-account and capital-account operations are fully convertible, with no exchange-rate risk exposure to a domestic fiat currency. Profit remittances and dividend distributions are freely payable abroad without prior exchange-control approval, but are subject to documentary AML/CFT due diligence by local banks, transfer-pricing review, and, where applicable, 5% dividend withholding tax (or 0% to 10% for shareholders in certain international foundations, depending on source and treaty relief). The principal residual hurdles are bank-level source-of-funds verification, tax-residency certificates, and economic-substance disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion timeline, or prescribed retention percentage in Panama. Export receipts may remain in USD, be deposited in external bank accounts, or be converted to any freely traded currency at market rates. The only obligations are documentary (invoices, bills of lading, shipping certificates) for tax, customs and SBP financial intelligence evidence; an exporter is not required to repatriate funds to a local account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise or Revolut Business are not licensed by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá and cannot independently host Panamanian-account numbers or IBAN equivalents. They may operate only as unregulated payment initiators cooperating with an SBP-licensed bank, and their acceptance for the PIF grocery operation is restricted to auxiliary functions. A fully licensed Panamanian bank account remains mandatory for ring-fenced capital, treasury operations, and supplier settlements in Asia.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC interview is generally required for at least one director or the founder of the Private Interest Foundation at most tier-1 Panamanian banks during initial onboarding. A dual-track mandate applies: (i) strict face-to-face identification for beneficial owners and founding council members; and (ii) remote opening is only permitted when documents are notarized and apostilled in the client's jurisdiction, and a third-party professional (Panamanian lawyer or trust company) certifies identity over a contemporaneous video call. In practice, physical attendance remains the most bankable path for a PIF with non-resident founders; alternative digital KYC must be approved in advance by the bank's Compliance Officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident founder with nominee/unexercised directorship in the PIF
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated foundation charter and registered statutes, full register of foundation members and beneficiaries, notarized and apostilled passports, sworn declaration of the foundation's commercial purpose, physical retail lease agreement for the supermarket, and bank reference letters from the founder's primary regulated institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds originating from an OFAC-sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete wire-trail file with SWIFT statements, audited financial statements, source-of-wealth declaration, regulatory licence for the grocery operation, tax clearances from the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), and a negative sanctions-screening report generated by a recognised compliance database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation lacking verifiable economic substance or physical footprint in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RUC (tax-ID) registration, municipal business licence, lease or purchase title for the warehouse/retail location, payroll and social security filings, import purchase orders and vendor invoices, inventory stock-taking reports, and a substance memorandum compliant with Law 70/2019 and Economic Substance Law 254/2019.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single-council structure / absence of local directorship creating shell-suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Appointment of at least two Panamanian resident council members, directors' service contracts, board resolutions approving treasury policies, quarterly management accounts and balance-sheet notes demonstrating third-party director oversight.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections are executed by SWIFT MT103 wires using the USD clearing network. The sender must reference either 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION' or 'INVESTMENT IN RETAIL TRADE — ISIC 4721' in the payment details; the receiving Panamanian bank verifies the transaction against the account's stated business, performs a live source-of-funds check and an OFAC/FATF filter, and records the inbound amount for DGI statistics. No prior approval from the SBP is required; however, the bank may request the foundation's capital-escrow ledger, the current corporate register entry, and proof of the grocery hub's active RUC registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements to Asian condiment and vegetable suppliers are cleared by (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for letters of payment against invoices under USD 5,000,000 per transaction; or (ii) irrevocable, confirming-house-backed Commercial Letters of Credit (CAD: original documents from the beneficiary's bank) for major procurement cycles. Each payment file must carry the trade invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, packing list, phytosanitary certificate, and, where applicable, a certificate of origin. Settlement takes place in USD via correspondent accounts; no local central-bank conversion step exists because the USD is legal tender.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for RMB-denominated procurement contracts
USD/JPY deliverable forward contracts and OTC currency-option collars for Japanese-source seasoning imports
Cross-currency swaps (USD vs CNH/JPY) for committed quarterly purchasing volumes
FX swap and overnight-swap lines with SBP-licensed banks for short-term working-capital conversion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual legal entity franchise tax (Pago Anual de Persona Jurídica)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) via the single tax account; payment administered by the Public Registry of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: June 15 of each year (next business day if on a weekend)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: USD 300 late surcharge if unpaid after June 15; extended delinquency may cause suspension of legal status and administrative strike-off after two consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración de Renta ISR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following each completed fiscal year (calendar year basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: 10% of assessed tax plus monthly interest at 1% per month; DGI may also impose additional fines and commence software-based or desk tax determination.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (Ministry of Economy and Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 90 calendar days after the foundation's registration anniversary (or per the published RUB calendar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 1,000 for late filing or inaccuracy; repeated non-compliance may result in suspension or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Resident agent and registered office annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama through the resident agent; statutory records of the Foundation Council
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of foundation charter registration; renewal per the Foundation service agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Termination of the resident agent without replacement within 30 days triggers administrative strike-off of the foundation from the Public Registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent financial audit is compulsory when annual gross revenue exceeds USD 3,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000; audited financial statements must accompany the income tax return. DGI may also require an audit for entities designated as large taxpayers or with transfer-pricing obligations. The Foundation Council may voluntarily order an audit for internal governance purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama mandates International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS/NIIF) as issued by the IFRS Foundation; SMEs may apply IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para las PYMES). No separate local GAAP is permitted for statutory financial reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council must file an annual UBO confirmation through DGI's Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB), covering each individual who owns or controls the foundation, including the founder and each current beneficiary. The resident agent must verify and preserve the private foundation register and certify that the UBO declaration is current. Any change in rights, transfer of foundation interests, or substitution of beneficiaries must be reported to the resident agent and updated in the RUB within 15 business days. A PIF does not issue shares, so no share-register confirmation protocol applies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Charter and By-Laws
Register of Foundation Council Members (appointment, revocation, and minutes)
Register of Founder and Beneficiaries (confidential UBO/trust register)
Register of Foundation Assets and Liabilities
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – 1,500 (depending on agent and filing volume)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 5,000 for a small retail operation, subject to DGI/IFRS requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on net taxable income exceeding PAB/USD 50,000; 15% on the first PAB/USD 50,000 (Panama Fiscal Code Art. 699).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral tax holiday applies to ISIC 4721 grocery retail. The Private Interest Foundation (PIF) benefits from the territorial sourcing rule under which non-Panamanian source income is outside the ISR base. Under Law 25 of 1995 Art. 23, the initial endowment and asset transfers into the PIF are exempt from Panama transfer taxes, but Panama-source commercial profits from the Asian supermarket are taxable at the ordinary 15%/25% scale with no additional statutory incentive.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 120 (Declaracion Jurada de Renta - Persona Juridica); mandatory electronic filing through the DGI Sistema T@S / SIME e-filing portal with a digital certificate; the PIF must hold an active RUC and a commercial Aviso de Operacion.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, complemented by quarterly ISR advance payments (anticipos) for the running fiscal year; ancillary monthly obligations include ITBMS (7%) returns, employee ISR withholdings, and CSS (Social Security) withholdings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within 3 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year taxpayers: 31 March) per Fiscal Code Art. 712; the DGI routinely grants a 2-month electronic extension (to 31 May) provided the balance due is paid under the published extension terms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registro Unico de Contribuyentes identification number and legal name of the Private Interest Foundation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign founders must instruct the Panama resident agent to obtain the PIF RUC and to appoint the resident agent as fiscal representative; a foreign address alone is not acceptable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax classification and commercial activity code: ISIC 4721 / CIIU 4721 (retail sale of food in specialized stores - Asian supermarket grocery hub).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declared activity must match the licensed Aviso de Operacion and municipal business license; any mismatch constitutes a filing red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue from Panama-source sales of the grocery hub, excluding non-Panamanian source income under the territorial rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cash and POS card sales must be fully recorded through a certified fiscal register integrated with SIME; unreported cash sales attract presumptive assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of imported Asian goods, rent, payroll, utilities, depreciation, and selling expenses supported by valid invoices and proof of withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions for payments to affiliated non-resident suppliers are disallowed unless transfer-pricing documentation and the 12.5% technical-service/royalty withholding (or treaty relief) are evidenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source receipts less allowed deductions, adjusted per Fiscal Code Art. 699 and including the net operating loss carryforward offset (maximum 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards may be used exclusively against Panama-source income; losses of foreign branches cannot be offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computed at 15% on the first PAB/USD 50,000 of net taxable income and 25% on the excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The determined tax becomes the basis for the 10% dividend withholding at the time of repatriation to the foreign founder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net payment after deducting quarterly advance payments (anticipos), creditable ITBMS, and third-party withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A claimed tax credit requires audited reconciliation; refund requests trigger a DGI desk audit and cannot be offset against foreign taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment trigger: (a) a 10% surcharge on the balance due for the first month or fraction of delay; (b) an additional 1% per month (or fraction) up to a 25% ceiling; (c) moratory interest of 1% per month; and (d) a fixed administrative fine of USD 500-1,000 per unfiled or false return under Fiscal Code Art. 713, plus criminal exposure under the evasion rules.
